content: The coadministration of medications that induce fluid and electrolyte imbalances can elevate the risk of adverse events such as seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Magnesium sulfate and potassium chloride have specific interactions with various drugs, as detailed below: 1. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and diflunisal: This combination increases the toxicity of diflunisal through an unspecified mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 2. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and digoxin: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride reduces digoxin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Administer digoxin at least 2 hours before or no less than 6 hours after magnesium to avoid chelation. 3. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and calcium channel blockers: Elevated serum magnesium concentrations in patients receiving calcium channel blockers may lead to hypotension or muscle weakness. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and disopyramide: This combination increases the toxicity of disopyramide by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Consider preand post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at higher risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 5. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and dofetilide: This combination increases the toxicity of dofetilide by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Preand post-colonoscopy ECGs should be considered for at-risk patients. 6. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and dolutegravir: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride reduces dolutegravir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Administer dolutegravir at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium to avoid chelation. 7. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and doxepin: This combination enhances the effects of doxepin through an unknown mechanism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 8. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and drugs that lower the seizure threshold: When used with high doses of magnesium sulfate, there is an increased risk of seizures. Close monitoring is required. 9. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and doxercalciferol: Doxercalciferol may enhance the hypermagnesemic effect of magnesium salts. Caution is advised. 10. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride and doxycycline: Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride reduces doxycycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug.
